diet.text: Mostly small mammals; also birds, lizards and eggs

overview.text: The Four-lined Snake is a non-venomous rat snake of Italy and the Balkans and one of the largest snakes in Europe.

identification.text: Adults are yellowish-brown with four dark stripes along the body and a black line from the eye to the corner of the mouth. Young ones look quite different: pale brown with dark blotches.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Italy (north to Tuscany and Umbria), coastal Slovenia and Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania, western Greece with many islands, and south-western Bulgaria.

habitat.text: Mediterranean places with plants, stone walls, open woodland, forest edges and old buildings. In winter small groups shelter in old rodent burrows.

diet.text: Mostly small mammals such as rabbits, squirrels and mice, plus birds, lizards, baby tortoises and eggs.

recognise.text: Four dark stripes along a yellowish-brown body (adults).
